novelty_claim: We introduce and empirically evaluate a diagnostic framework for Semantic Causal Pathway Consistency in multimodal language models. Given an image and question, we identify question-critical visual evidence and recover an approximate minimal set of attention-head mediators that restore a fixed candidate answer under evidence deletion. We measure whether the same semantic evidence, across human-validated meaning-preserving variants, retains a stable internal causal pathway. The framework combines external evidence effects (CECA), cross-variant mediator consistency (CPS), and their joint score (SCC = CECA × CPS).
primary_research_question: Among examples whose answer remains correct and behaviorally invariant under reviewed semantic-preserving image changes, how often does the recovered attention-head mediator set vary, and does joint external/internal pathway measurement predict failure on a disjoint reviewed transformation family beyond behavioral, confidence, grounding, CLIP, and external-necessity baselines?
primary_measure: scc = distribution_ceca * weighted_cps; calculate only when both component measures are defined
candidate_answer_protocol: Freeze a question-specific answer-bin list before any model inference and without consulting gold answers or model predictions. Include all plausible answer bins plus an explicit other/unknown bin. Store the frozen list and protocol string in the reviewed manifest.
split_protocol: Assign image groups to analysis train/validation/test before evidence review. Keep all questions, variants, masks, and outputs from an image in one split. Fit/calibrate on train only; use validation only for declared threshold choices; report test once.
variant_protocol: Human review every used variant for answer preservation, critical evidence preservation, relation preservation, and audit completion. Assign probe and heldout roles before model execution; transformation families must not overlap across roles.
failure_outcome: For baseline-correct items only, failure is a VQA consensus score below 0.5 on at least one heldout approved variant. Also report answer-flip outcomes separately. This outcome is transformation-family generalization, not general OOD or hallucination detection.
required_ablations: blur vs gray vs inpaint intervention
greedy vs exact mediator search on small candidate sets
sample_size_note: Target is provisional. Recompute using pilot variance, failure prevalence, and a prospective power or precision analysis before confirmatory collection.
claim_boundary: Report intervention effects on model outputs and approximate attention-head mediation. Do not claim true reasoning circuits, hallucination reduction, general OOD prediction, or causal truth from SCC alone.
